name: Crowley Santo Tomas de Castilla Container Terminal - Guatemala

fieldNotes.yardSpots: The trailerParkingCapacity figure (~2,200) is a CONTAINER / CHASSIS GROUND-SLOT estimate, not OTR trailer stalls. Counted from z18-z20 satellite over the Crowley/EmpresaPortuaria stacking yard: dense multi-row ground slots of stacked containers plus chassis/trailer lanes along the apron. Marine terminal, so OTR dock doors are near-zero; the dock-door count reflects the attached warehouse.
fieldNotes.attachedWarehouse: Crowley operates a +350,000 sqft warehouse / transit shed here (24/7 per Crowley). The large pale roof shed on the east side of the terminal (z19) is the warehouse; its landward face carries the truck loading doors counted in dockDoorCount (0-10 band, ~10, low confidence at this resolution).
fieldNotes.siteIdentification: Confirmed against Crowley + Empresa Portuaria Nacional Santo Tomas de Castilla pages and port references (lat ~15.69-15.71, lng ~-88.616). z16-z20 satellite shows the multipurpose/container terminal on Amatique Bay: ship-to-shore + ship gear at the quay, dense container ground slots, a large transit-shed warehouse, terminal tractors and chassis. CA-9 highway and the town of Santo Tomas sit immediately landward.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Inferred from layout: the terminal is a fully fenced port estate with a single landward access road off CA-9, the standard secured-gate configuration for a Central American container port. Specific gate hardware not resolved in available imagery - flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Inferred (secured national port). Specific guard booth not positively resolved - flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.scale: Weighbridge is standard at this terminal (Crowley publishes Guatemala export weight restrictions enforced at gate), so scale=true is inferred, not visually confirmed - flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 50+ band: the container/chassis stacking yard holds many hundreds to ~2,000+ ground slots.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur into the terminal resolved; Guatemala's Atlantic rail is largely inactive. railServed=false.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Small port town (Santo Tomas de Castilla / Puerto Barrios) on a narrow Caribbean coast - classified Rural per rubric (small-town industrial -> Rural).
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus-scale: quay/transit sheds, the +350k sqft warehouse, container stacking yards, and ancillary port buildings.
fieldNotes.streetView: Nearest Street View is a 2018-04 user photosphere (pano CAoS...E1rj_Fw) on the public access road ~280m SW of the terminal centroid; no Google car road coverage inside the secured port. heading 66 deg points from the pano toward the terminal.
